newsitem.title: USA: Extra Colo. River flows lift power output 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Extra Colo. River flows lift power output 15 pct.

text.p: This year's healthy precipitation and extra releases through Lower Colorado River hydropower projects will boost power generation by around 15 percent, according to the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, which operates the dams.

In a normal water year, power output from Hoover, Davis and Parker Dams totals about 6 million megawatt hours (MWh), but this year they are expected to generate 6.9 million MWh, spokesman Bob Walsh said Tuesday.
Reclamation began at the end of July to release extra water through the dams in a bid to clear space for winter inflows to Lake Mead, which is behind Hoover Dam in Nevada and Arizona.
The souped-up flows, currently averaging 18,000 cubic feet per second (cfs) from Hoover and Davis and 16,000 cfs from Parker, are scheduled to continue through mid-September.
Total power generating capacity at Hoover Dam is 2,080 megawatts (MW), 240 MW at Davis and 120 MW at Parker.

In mid-September, the releases are expected to return to more typical levels of 11,000 to 12,000 cfs from Hoover, 11,500 cfs from Davis and 8,000 to 9,500 cfs from Parker and to remain at those rates or lower through autumn.
Elevation of Lake Mead, currently near 1,204 feet above sea level, is expected to gradually rise to around 1,210 feet by the end of December.
Reclamation is projecting a 70 percent likelihood that flood control releases of about 20,000 cfs from Hoover Dam will be necessary starting in January.
